taxa.name: Drosera albonotata
taxa.dist: Western Wheatbelt: Wandoo National Park and the Northam, York and Quairading shires.
taxa.hab: Sandy clay-loam on gravelly slopes, ridges and low rises in Wandoo woodland.
taxa.note: Described 2018, after Nunn & Lambers' soil table.

taxa.name: Drosera allantostigma
taxa.dist: A few roadside sites near Hill River, north of Perth.
taxa.hab: Loam, silica sand or peaty sand on the edges of winter-wet depressions.

taxa.name: Drosera androsacea
taxa.dist: South of Perth: Corrigin, Dragon Rocks, Katanning, Stirling Range, Varley and Williams.
taxa.hab: Exposed, poor, often compacted or clayey soils in Wheatbelt mallee and low heath: stony white sandy loam or loam with laterite gravel. These soils bake hard in summer.

taxa.name: Drosera australis
taxa.dist: A narrow strip along the south coast from Augusta to east of Esperance.
taxa.hab: Wet spots in coastal heath, such as the edges of seasonally flooded swampy hollows; also sandy soil over laterite nearby.

taxa.name: Drosera barbigera
taxa.dist: Two areas: Eneabba to York, and around Dumbleyung and Lake Grace.
taxa.hab: White silica sand and laterite gravel on the slopes and tops of laterite hills. Moist only while winter rain lasts; dries out in summer.

taxa.name: Drosera bindoon
taxa.dist: A 40 km stretch between Muchea and Wannamal.
taxa.hab: Heavy, rough laterite gravel on hillsides and hilltops.

taxa.name: Drosera callistos
taxa.dist: Around Gidgegannup and the state forest along the Brookton Highway.
taxa.hab: Heavy laterite-covered sand, and pockets of pure sand surrounded by laterite.

taxa.name: Drosera citrina
taxa.dist: Regans Ford (Moore River) and Boonanarring, north of Perth.
taxa.hab: Well-drained deep yellow sand in open heath or under Banksia woodland.
taxa.note: Includes D. coalara, merged into this species in 2020.

taxa.name: Drosera closterostigma
taxa.dist: Gingin to Cataby, east toward Mogumber.
taxa.hab: Deep white sand grayed by humus, often in winter-wet depressions and swampy heath.

taxa.name: Drosera coomallo
taxa.dist: Badgingarra, Cataby and Coomallo.
taxa.hab: Laterite pebbles over laterite sheet rock on the upper slopes of hills.

taxa.name: Drosera depauperata
taxa.dist: Only its type site: Lake Pleasant View near Manypeaks.
taxa.hab: Lake edges and wet depressions in sandy soil under paperbarks.

taxa.name: Drosera dichrosepala
taxa.dist: Near Woodanilling and between Katanning and Nyabing.
taxa.hab: Well-drained shallow sand over laterite with laterite pebbles, among low scrub.

taxa.name: Drosera echinoblastus
taxa.dist: Hill River, Coomallo and Mount Lesueur, extending north and south.
taxa.hab: Deep white sand or beige clayey sand beside winter-wet streams, depressions and seeps.

taxa.name: Drosera eneabba
taxa.dist: Eneabba, Badgingarra, Coomallo and Mount Lesueur.
taxa.hab: Deep, well-drained white silica sand in low open heath, often under sparse shrubs.

taxa.name: Drosera enodes
taxa.dist: The far south-west corner: Scott River and Windy Harbour.
taxa.hab: Black peaty sand on swamp edges.

taxa.name: Drosera gibsonii
taxa.dist: Near the base of Bluff Knoll in the Stirling Range.
taxa.hab: Granite and laterite scree on the lower slopes of the Stirling Range, laterite on the plains between peaks, and clayey sand on watershed slopes.

taxa.name: Drosera grievei
taxa.dist: Hilly country inland of Ravensthorpe: Lake Grace east to Baanga Hill, and around Lake King and Newdegate.
taxa.hab: Beige sandy clay with a little laterite, in low open heath.

taxa.name: Drosera helodes
taxa.dist: Bullsbrook, Byford, Muchea and Gingin.
taxa.hab: Gray sand in winter-wet depressions, and black humic sand on seasonal swamp edges.

taxa.name: Drosera hyperostigma
taxa.dist: Darling Range: Bannister, Gidgegannup, Lesmurdie, Parkerville and The Lakes.
taxa.hab: Well-drained laterite mixed with silica sand in open, light forest.

taxa.name: Drosera lasiantha
taxa.dist: Porongurup Range and Mount Lindesay, near Albany and Denmark.
taxa.hab: Loamy laterite scree on high slopes in low jarrah forest, and skeletal soil on granite.

taxa.name: Drosera leioblastus
taxa.dist: The Cataby region.
taxa.hab: Silica sand with leaf-litter humus and laterite pebbles, under low heath.
taxa.dormNote: Reported under its older name, D. placenta subsp. leioblasta.

taxa.name: Drosera leucoblasta
taxa.dist: York, Brookton, Cranbrook, Arthur River and Esperance.
taxa.hab: Clayey sand, clay and laterite between low shrubs in heath; soils often carry organic matter and peat.

taxa.name: Drosera leucostigma
taxa.dist: Cataby region, south-east to Mogumber.
taxa.hab: Sandy soils on the edges of winter-wet depressions.

taxa.name: Drosera mannii
taxa.dist: Gleneagle, Boulder Rock and toward Jarrahdale.
taxa.hab: Loam in jarrah forest, peaty sand on winter-wet seeps, and granite-outcrop aprons.

taxa.name: Drosera micra
taxa.dist: Known from Malaga, in Perth's northern suburbs (its type locality). Listed Priority One flora in WA.
taxa.hab: Black sandy soil in winter-wet swampland.
taxa.note: Can form a dormant bud in summer but usually just slows its growth (Lowrie & Conran 2014). Climate is from its single known site.

taxa.name: Drosera micrantha
taxa.dist: Common from Perth to Albany.
taxa.hab: White silica sand on the higher edges of swamps, and deep sand pockets in the Darling Range.

taxa.name: Drosera microscapa
taxa.dist: Denmark, Hortons, Manypeaks and Frenchman Bay.
taxa.hab: Black silty sand in seepage areas of swampy heath.

taxa.name: Drosera miniata
taxa.dist: Gidgegannup, Toodyay and York.
taxa.hab: Laterite, clay and silty clay on slopes, often exposed and near granite outcrops; also loam washed onto granite aprons.

taxa.name: Drosera minutiflora
taxa.dist: Cataby, Mogumber, Wanneroo, Gnangarra and The Lakes.
taxa.hab: Deep white silica sand between low shrubs in heath.

taxa.name: Drosera nitidula
taxa.dist: East of Perth, south to Augusta and east to Cape Le Grand.
taxa.hab: Clayey sand in and around winter-wet depressions and swamps.

taxa.name: Drosera nivea
taxa.dist: Only around Coorow.
taxa.hab: Deep pale yellow to beige sand on sandplain heath.

taxa.name: Drosera occidentalis
taxa.dist: Gingin, Bullsbrook, Perth, Pinjarra and Carbarup.
taxa.hab: Peaty sand around swamp edges, winter-wet depressions and seeps.

taxa.name: Drosera omissa
taxa.dist: Widespread: Kalbarri to Ravensthorpe.
taxa.hab: Deep white sand around winter-wet depressions; occasionally laterite.

taxa.name: Drosera oreopodion
taxa.dist: The foot of the Darling Range.
taxa.hab: Sandy clay mixed with laterite pebbles in low heath.

taxa.name: Drosera paleacea
taxa.dist: Albany area: Lake Sepping, Princess Royal Harbour, Frenchman Bay, Little Grove.
taxa.hab: Black sand among reeds and paperbarks on flats that flood in winter.

taxa.name: Drosera patens
taxa.dist: Four sites across Perth's northern suburbs, plus Manaring Lake.
taxa.hab: Sandy edges of swamps, lakes and winter-wet depressions.

taxa.name: Drosera pedicellaris
taxa.dist: South-west of Three Springs, with sites near Badgingarra and Nambung.
taxa.hab: Deep beige to white sand between low shrubs in heath.

taxa.name: Drosera platystigma
taxa.dist: Albany, Bannister, Busselton, Pinjarra, Stirling Range, Ravensthorpe.
taxa.hab: Clayey sand, laterite or loam in open heath and jarrah-forest clearings.

taxa.name: Drosera pulchella
taxa.dist: Perth, Augusta, Albany and Esperance.
taxa.hab: Sand, peaty sand, peat, laterite or loam on the edges of lakes, swamps, streams and seeps; sometimes grows submerged.

taxa.name: Drosera pycnoblasta
taxa.dist: Pingelly, Tammin, Goomalling and the Lake King area.
taxa.hab: Deep white sand, clayey white sand over laterite gravel, or yellow sand, in low heath and mallee.

taxa.name: Drosera pygmaea
taxa.dist: South-eastern Australia and New Zealand; in WA only near Albany and Karridale.
taxa.hab: A wide range of poor soils, usually near winter water: seeps, trailside ditches, peaty swamp edges, and shallow sand or clay in exposed heath.
taxa.note: Climate covers the whole range, not just WA.

taxa.name: Drosera rechingeri
taxa.dist: Kalbarri, Ajana, Binnu, Mingenew and Dongara.
taxa.hab: Deep white or yellow sand in open heath.

taxa.name: Drosera roseana
taxa.dist: South coast from Albany to Augusta.
taxa.hab: Peaty sand on swamp edges.

taxa.name: Drosera sargentii
taxa.dist: Esperance to Cape Le Grand and Cape Arid.
taxa.hab: Deep, fine white silica sand in low coastal heath and on consolidated dunes.

taxa.name: Drosera scorpioides
taxa.dist: Albany, Manypeaks, Bowelling and Gidgegannup.
taxa.hab: Pebbly laterite outcrops with a little silica sand, among heath and open woodland.
taxa.dormNote: One grower reports that plants which go dormant rarely come back, so it is worth keeping this one in active growth.

taxa.name: Drosera sewelliae
taxa.dist: Chittering Valley, Muchea and Toodyay.
taxa.hab: Laterite with silica sand in open forest, and laterite over sheet rock.

taxa.name: Drosera silvicola
taxa.dist: Avon Valley, North Bannister and Boddington.
taxa.hab: Laterite rubble among leaf litter on the slopes and summits of high hills in jarrah forest.

taxa.name: Drosera spilos
taxa.dist: Widespread: Walkaway south to Bannister, inland to Wyalkatchem.
taxa.hab: Loam strewn with laterite pebbles, or clayey sand, often near granite outcrops.

taxa.name: Drosera stelliflora
taxa.dist: Jarrah forest between Busselton and Margaret River.
taxa.hab: Laterite soils, sometimes with a little silica sand.

taxa.name: Drosera trichocaulis
taxa.dist: Stirling Range east along the coast to Cape Arid.
taxa.hab: Deep white sand, or laterite and sand, under low heath and open woodland.

taxa.name: Drosera verrucata
taxa.dist: Common from Albany to Manypeaks.
taxa.hab: Clayey sand between low shrubs in heath and scrub; also roadside gravel.

taxa.name: Drosera walyunga
taxa.dist: Walyunga National Park and nearby.
taxa.hab: Sandy white clay with a thin laterite gravel layer, around winter-wet springs and seeps.

taxa.name: Drosera × badgerupii
taxa.dist: Western Australia. Now extinct in the wild.
taxa.hab: Peaty sand or pure peat on swamp and lake edges.
taxa.note: Known only in cultivation; no climate shown.

taxa.name: Drosera × badgingarra
taxa.dist: Only its type site at Badgingarra.
taxa.hab: Clay-rich sand on the edges of wet depressions.

taxa.name: Drosera × carbarup
taxa.dist: Only its type site at Carbarup, near Mount Barker.
taxa.hab: Laterite and sand in winter-wet depressions with dwarf paperbarks.
taxa.note: Sterile. One grower source gives D. nitidula × D. occidentalis instead.

taxa.name: Drosera × legrandii
taxa.dist: Only its type site at Cape Le Grand.
taxa.hab: Black silty sand in swampy heath.

taxa.name: Drosera × pingellyensis
taxa.dist: Only its type site near Pingelly.
taxa.hab: White sand on the edges of wet depressions.

taxa.name: Drosera × sidjamesii
taxa.dist: Shores of a few lakes north of Perth.
taxa.hab: Silica sand stabilised by sedges on lake shores; sometimes underwater in wet winters.

icps.t: ICPS Guide to the Pygmy Drosera (after Lowrie et al. 2017)
